The only reason to introduce `legacy_keyboard_mouse_device_ids`, is to fix a bug and it will need to be supported until the end of Godot V4 or risk a compatibility breaking change.
Personally I'm not sure, if that is enough of a reason for introducing such a project setting.
Have you checked, if there are any other project settings in Godot4, that have the single purpose of fixing a bug? If that is not the case, then I would like to suggest to perhaps consider other approaches.

> The only reason to introduce `legacy_keyboard_mouse_device_ids`, is to fix a bug and it will need to be supported until the end of Godot V4 or risk a compatibility breaking change. Personally I'm not sure, if that is enough of a reason for introducing such a project setting. Have you checked, if there are any other project settings in Godot4, that have the single purpose of fixing a bug? If that is not the case, then I would like to suggest to perhaps consider other approaches.

This was already a breaking change. It is the kind of stuff that both needs to be warned as a breaking change in the blogposts and just overall the kind of stuff you wouldn't introduce until 5.0. None of which happened.  
  
Keep in mind that ANY project relying on input IDs breaks with this change. Which has always been the main way to differentiate devices without creating an InputMap entry for each separate device.  
  
This PR is a correction to that breaking change.

> The only reason to introduce `legacy_keyboard_mouse_device_ids`, is to fix a bug and it will need to be supported until the end of Godot V4 or risk a compatibility breaking change.
> Personally I'm not sure, if that is enough of a reason for introducing such a project setting.
> Have you checked, if there are any other project settings in Godot4, that have the single purpose of fixing a bug? If that is not the case, then I would like to suggest to perhaps consider other approaches.

Now that I think about it, there are at least 2 ways to look at the problem of keyboards and mice having id of 0: either it was intentional before but not documented, or it was a bug but the documentation didn't mention that the IDs of devices can change in later Godot versions, if that makes sense.
Personally, I think it was a bug, but keeping compatibility is important, so having a project setting makes the most sense. (Or we can ask the people to make changes to their projects according to this change, if that's realistic and viable?)
What do you think?

> > Keep in mind that ANY project relying on input IDs breaks with this change. Which has always been the main way to differentiate devices without creating an InputMap entry for each separate device.
> 
> I'm a bit confused now. Before the device ID change keyboards and mice had id of 0, which doesn't allow to differentiate them from other devices via the ids alone. And this change shouldn't affect InputMap, since InputMap doesn't allow the developer to specify the device ID for keyboard and mouse, and if keyboard or mouse events with id of 0 get added to InputMap, the ids are automatically adjusted to the new ones. 😅 @NancokPS2

I think the common practice this PR is trying not to break is mapping the device id 0 to player 1, for example, in a multiplayer setting. @NancokPS2

> > Keep in mind that ANY project relying on input IDs breaks with this change. Which has always been the main way to differentiate devices without creating an InputMap entry for each separate device.
>

And this change shouldn't affect InputMap, since InputMap doesn't allow the developer to specify the device ID for keyboard and mouse, and if keyboard or mouse events with id of 0 get added to InputMap, the ids are automatically adjusted to the new ones. 😅 @NancokPS2

Right. Which means that existing code relies on treating both the mouse and keyboard as being at the same ID, basically treating the ID as being one for each player. (Since nobody is going to play with a keyboard just to give someone else the mouse)  
I am not saying this is a bad change at all btw. But it IS a breaking change and it is not announced anywhere.  
Everyone could go back and rework all their input code for this. After magically realizing this change was made at some point.  
And yes, this is a mald comment. I spent quite a bunch of hours trying to figure out why all my inputs stopped working. (no shade to anyone btw, this IS a dev release after all)
